Fixed. Verifier is now declared as pub struct Verifier<'a, V, R, A = NoAiaFetcher>.

The bead was correct and the case is the textbook one for C-STRUCT-BOUNDS: every field is a shared reference (&'a V, &'a R, &'a A, &'a [TrustAnchor], &'a ValidationPolicy) plus a Copy AiaConfig, so none of the three traits affects the data representation. Both inherent impls already declared the bounds in their own where clauses, so nothing moved -- the struct-level copies were pure duplication.

Not a breaking change: relaxing a bound only widens what can be named, and callers could never have constructed a non-conforming Verifier anyway since new() requires the traits.

Clone, Copy and Debug dropped the bounds entirely rather than restating them. None needed them: Debug prints the anchor count, policy and config, and copying a bundle of shared references is free whatever they point at.

Side benefit worth noting: this made the existing compile-time assertion strictly stronger. It previously instantiated Verifier over a type implementing the three traits and nothing else -- the most the struct bounds permitted -- and now uses a type implementing NOTHING. One assertion now guards both properties: reinstating a struct bound fails to compile, and replacing the hand-written Clone/Copy with a #[derive] fails too (a derive would add V: Copy bounds the struct does not need, holding &V rather than V).

Verified by mutation: reinstating V: SignatureVerifier on the struct fails the build at the Clone impl with "the trait bound `V: SignatureVerifier` is not satisfied".

Also removed the capability traits from _verifier_is_send_sync, which only ever needed Sync (&T is Send exactly when T is Sync).

Related and still open: PKIX-sqek.19, on whether the three named generics should become a single trust-domain seam. That is an API-shape question and is untouched here -- this change only removes redundancy, it does not alter the parameter list.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, 2345 tests.
